model.title: Model (JSON)
model.detail: BuEM GeoJSON: everything a simulation needs

view.detached: This building's saved surfaces come from an earlier City2TABULA generation, so none matches the current 3D data. The saved values still apply; the model is not shown.
view.noGeometry: City2TABULA holds no 3D geometry for this building.

discardSurface.message: You changed this surface. Keep the changes?
discardSurface.note: Discarding puts the surface back as it was when its editor opened.

panel.empty: Click a surface in the model to see it here.

surface.uValueTip: How much heat passes through one m² of this surface per degree of difference between inside and outside. It comes from TABULA for this building's type, age and refurbishment level; a lower value loses less heat, so the building needs less heating.

profile.title: Hourly load profile

error.unreadable: Could not parse load profile file.

profile.uploadSoon: Custom consumption profile uploads will be available soon.
profile.downloadTip: Download the hourly heating, cooling, electricity, hot water and cooking gas profiles as one CSV

pv.hint: Click a roof or wall to set up PV, or drop a product on it.

card.fromModel: Tilt, facing and area come from the building's 3D model.
card.noFit: No whole module fits on this surface.
card.spaceLimited: The space on this surface limits the modules; a larger usable share adds none.

mounting.label: Mounting
mounting.tip: How the panels sit on a flat roof. {flush}: they lie flat on the roof. {racked}: they stand on frames at the tilt and facing you set, so they catch more sun but need more space between rows.

orientation.label: Format
orientation.tip: Which way the panels are turned on the surface. {portrait}: the long side runs up the surface. {landscape}: the long side runs across it. {auto} uses whichever way fits the most panels, mixing both where that fits more.

cost.estimateNote: Estimates from the products’ costs, before a simulation.

catalogue.hint: Drag a product onto a roof or wall, or choose one in a surface’s panel.
catalogue.drag: Drag onto a roof or wall in the model
catalogue.name: Photovoltaic options

values.buildingOnly: Changes to {name} apply to this building only.

question.cost_energy_cap: What does it cost per kWp?
question.cost_om_annual: What is the yearly upkeep per kWp?
question.cont_lifetime: How many years does it last?

values.saveFailed: Could not save the technology. Try again.

pv.followsModel: PV follows the 3D model's {tilt}°; the tilt and facing edited above go to BuEM only.

noFitOn.one: No whole PV module fits on {surfaces}, so it has no PV. Choose a smaller product or another surface.
noFitOn.other: No whole PV module fits on {count} surfaces ({surfaces}), so they have no PV. Choose a smaller product or other surfaces.

help.title: How to add PV
help.drag: Open {options} and drag a product onto a roof or wall.
help.click: Select a roof or wall, switch on {install} and choose a product.
help.remove: Switch off {install} in the surface's panel or in {surfaces}.
help.all: Click {useSuggested} to add PV to every surface marked {suggested}.

moduleCount.label: Modules (up to {fits})
moduleCount.tip: How many modules to place on this surface, up to the number that fits in its usable share. The capacity follows from it.

pv.removeAll: Remove all PV from this building

unsized.one: Without {count} technology the optimiser sizes, whose cost follows from its size.
unsized.other: Without {count} technologies the optimiser sizes, whose cost follows from their size.

useMilp.label: Use MILP solver
useMilp.tip: Solve the thermal model as a mixed-integer linear programme instead of BuEM's default sparse solver. Slower, but handles inequality constraints exactly.

solver.milpNote: MILP solver: inequality constraints handled exactly. Runs take longer.

ignis.unsupportedAfter: is not in the TABULA database. Supported types: {types}.
ignis.noData: No TABULA data found for this building: the TABULA service holds no variant for it or could not be reached.
ignis.borrowed: {type} has no energy grades of its own. Those shown are a {from}'s of the same age and country and do not reflect a non-residential building, so the values can differ: check that they match the building.

expertMore.title: Thermal and simulation
expertMore.detail: profiles, equipment and solver keep their defaults

mass.label: Thermal mass
mass.tip: How much heat the structure stores. Light: timber frame or lightweight; medium: mixed; heavy: concrete or masonry.

capacity.label: Heat capacity per floor area
capacity.tip: Set from the thermal mass class; editable.

hotWater.label: Hot water
hotWater.tip: Turn off when hot water is supplied by a system accounted for elsewhere. Space heating is unaffected.

heating.label: Heating setpoint
heating.tip: Lowest indoor temperature the heating keeps.

setback.label: Lower it when
setback.tip: Lowers the heating setpoint while occupants are asleep or away. Affects heating only.

cooling.label: Cooling setpoint
cooling.tip: Highest indoor temperature the cooling keeps.
cooling.inverted: Set it above the heating setpoint.

infiltration.label: Air leakage
infiltration.tip: Uncontrolled air changes per hour through gaps in the envelope (infiltration).

use.label: Ventilation by occupants
use.tip: Air changes per hour from window opening and fans while the building is in use.

capacity.label: Capacity
capacity.tip: Number of people. Left empty, a typical number for the building's size and type is used.

dwellings.label: Dwellings
dwellings.requiredTip: Number of homes in the building, filled in from typical buildings of this type.
dwellings.tip: Number of homes in the building.

persons.label: Occupants per dwelling
persons.tip: People living in each dwelling. The default is the statistical household size for the country, region and building type.

archetype.label: Household type
archetype.tip: Household composition. Sets when occupants are at home, which drives internal gains, electricity and hot water.

region.label: Region code (Netherlands)
region.tip: Dutch CBS municipality code. Selects the regional household size when occupants per dwelling is left to the default.

cooking.label: Cooking with
cooking.tip: Electric cooking stays inside the electricity profile. Gas cooking is reported separately as cooking gas.

equipment.intro: Default leaves each appliance to BuEM's ownership statistics.
equipment.sameInEveryDwelling: Every dwelling in the building gets the same appliances.

outputs.cookingGasOnlyWithGas: Cooking gas is reported only when cooking with gas.
outputs.thermalOff: Without heating or cooling BuEM skips the thermal model: surfaces and weather are not used.

preset.label: Set the whole building to
preset.tip: Choose a level for the whole building. It sets every wall, roof, floor and window; surfaces you changed one by one keep their values.
preset.fromType: TABULA variants for the building type and age.

customKept.one: {count} surface set one by one keeps its value.
customKept.other: {count} surfaces set one by one keep their values.

table.title: Per element type
table.lossFactorTip: Share of the heat loss through these surfaces that counts: 1 to outdoor air, less against ground or an unheated space (BuEM b_transmission). Empty when the surfaces differ; party walls keep 0.

windows.title: Windows BuEM adds
windows.note: The building has no window surfaces, so BuEM glazes a share of each exposed wall.

share.label: Window share
share.tip: Share of each exposed wall's area that is glazed.

u.label: Window U
u.tip: U-value of those windows. Default: the TABULA value for the building type, else 2.8.

g.label: Window g
g.tip: Share of the sunlight on those windows that enters as heat. Default: the TABULA value for the building type, else 0.5.

classes.comparing: Working out the grade of each level…
classes.note: Indicative class: space heating per m², graded on one scale for every country (the Austrian HWB scale, G to A++), so buildings compare across countries. National labels such as the Dutch energy label grade primary energy, which this model does not compute. Simulated, not a certificate.
classes.failed: The energy classes could not be worked out.
classes.source: The refurbishment levels come from TABULA, the European building typology.

default.tabulaElse: The TABULA value for this building, else {value}

unsaved.title: Unsaved changes
unsaved.message: You have unsaved changes to this building configuration. What would you like to do?
unsaved.note: Closing without saving will discard all modifications made since the last save.

error.dwellingsRequired: This building type needs its number of dwellings. Set it under Occupancy before running a simulation.
error.runFailed: Simulation failed: the EnerPlanET backend is unreachable or rejected the request. See the browser console for details.
error.importFailed: Could not parse file: {reason}. Ensure it is a valid BuEM GeoJSON, legacy configurator export, or EnerPlanET config.json.
error.pvFailed: The PV run failed, so PV generation is not shown. The energy demand above is up to date.
error.dwellingsModelledRequired: Some storeys are left out of the model. Give the dwellings of every modelled storey under Storeys modelled before running a simulation.

storeys.title: Storeys modelled
storeys.hint: Storey 0 is the ground floor. Leave a storey out of the model, or give it its own height and dwellings, in its row; a row picked here or in the model is highlighted in both. Floor area and envelope count the modelled storeys only.
storeys.noGeometry: Storeys can be left out once the 3D model has loaded.
storeys.pickHint: Click storeys in the model to select them; set them in Storeys modelled on the Building tab.
storeys.lastOne: At least one storey stays in the model.
storeys.dwellingsMissing: Give the number of homes on every included storey. Missing: storey {storeys}.
storeys.roomHeightTip: The height of each storey, floor to floor. A storey given its own height keeps it.

limit.storeys: Another storey at {room} m would be taller than the 3D model, which is {height} m to the eaves.
limit.height: A taller storey would make the storeys taller than the 3D model, which is {height} m to the eaves.

storeys.heightConflict: The storeys are {total} m tall together, taller than the 3D model, which is {height} m to the eaves. Lower the storey count or a height.

attic.label: Attic
attic.hint: The space under the pitched roof, above the eaves. Left out, the roof leaves the heated building and the ceiling below it loses heat to the cold attic.
attic.floorAreaTip: Measured from the 3D model: floor counts in full where the roof is 2 m or more above it, half where it is 1 to 2 m above it.

help.envelope: The size of this surface and how well it keeps heat in. Changing them changes how much heating the building needs.
help.pv: Solar panels on this surface: switch them on, choose a product and set how much of the surface they may cover.
help.building: The basic facts about the building: its type, age, country, size and storeys. Use Edit to correct them.
help.demand: How much energy the building needs in a year, split by use. Gas for cooking is shown on its own and is not in the total.
help.insulation: How well the whole building keeps heat in, and the grade that gives it. Choose a level to see what refurbishment would change. Existing: the building as it is. Usual: a common refurbishment, such as roof insulation and new windows. Advanced: a deep refurbishment, close to a new building. Surfaces you changed one by one keep their own values.
help.occupancy: How many storeys the building has, which of them are included, and how many homes are on each. More people means more hot water and more warmth from inside.
help.comfort: When and how warm the building is kept: the indoor temperature, whether it is turned down at night or when nobody is home, and whether hot water is counted.
help.outputs: Which results you get for each use: a yearly total, an hourly profile, or none.
help.equipment: Which appliances the homes have. They decide the electricity use; appliances left unset use typical values.
help.solver: How the hourly results are worked out: the standard method, which is fast, or a slower one that keeps exactly to the set limits.

model.title: The building in 3D
model.body: Drag to turn the model, scroll to zoom. Click a wall, roof or floor to open it.

surface.title: One surface at a time
surface.body: The surface you click opens here: its area, U-value and windows, and its PV where it takes any.

building.title: The whole building
building.body: Its annual demand, its data and its parameters. A refurbishment level here changes every surface at once.

technologies.title: Technologies
technologies.body: PV, storage and heating on this building. Open the catalogue and drag a product onto a surface to install it.

run.title: Save and preview
run.body: Works out the building's energy demand as it is now and shows it hour by hour.

hints.step1: Click a wall, roof or floor to open it.
hints.step2: Change its area or U-value in the panel.
hints.step3: Save and preview to see the building's new demand.

tip.openDocs: Click for the default values in the documentation.
